system.name: Sandman
system.one_liner: a CPU scheduling framework for storage servers that scales I/O threads across cores to save power without hurting performance

components.name: Main Core
components.role: runs a Scheduler that gathers metrics and makes decisions to redistribute I/O threads among cores to save power

components.name: Worker Core
components.role: processes networking and storage I/O requests in polling mode and can receive migrated I/O threads from the scheduler

components.name: Scheduler
components.role: gathers metrics and makes decisions about redistributing I/O threads among cores

components.name: Event Queue
components.role: lets cores communicate, carrying scheduling events such as metric reports and migration decisions

components.name: I/O Thread
components.role: a lightweight thread processing networking/storage I/O that can quickly migrate between cores

components.name: NIC
components.role: a network device polled by a core's I/O thread for networking requests

components.name: SSD
components.role: a storage device polled by a core's I/O thread for storage requests

flows.what: gather metrics / get metric events reported to the scheduler
make decisions / mark move, a scheduling decision sent to a worker core
move thread, an I/O thread migrating between cores as directed by the scheduler
TX/RX and SQ/CQ I/O flow polled by the core's I/O thread
TX/RX and SQ/CQ I/O flow polled by the core's I/O thread

content.key_idea: One main core's scheduler gathers metrics from worker cores and migrates I/O threads between them to consolidate work and save power, without disrupting the underlying polling I/O path.
content.reading_order: Top legend first, then left-to-right across Main Core and Worker Cores, following blue scheduling arrows up top and black I/O arrows from the devices below.

palette.used_for: dusty pink/mauve fill for the inner component bars (Scheduler, Event Queue, I/O Thread) and the NIC/SSD device boxes
blue lines for the Scheduling Flow arrows (Gather metrics, Make decisions)
pale khaki/yellow-green fill for the outer Main Core and Worker Core container boxes

style.stroke: thin solid black outlines (~0.6pt) on all boxes
style.font: GillSans sans-serif, 7pt, mostly regular with a little bold for headings
style.arrows: thin black arrows for I/O flow between devices and cores, blue arrows for scheduling flow between cores, plus a bold black curved arrow for thread migration
style.icons: vector - alarm-clock icon for timed polling, circular-arrow icon for busy polling, reused next to each polled component

encoding.color_means: khaki = a CPU core's outer container box, dusty pink = the functional bars/devices inside a core or on the device row; color otherwise does not distinguish role
encoding.line_style_means: black arrows = I/O Flow (device traffic into cores), blue arrows = Scheduling Flow (metrics and migration decisions between cores); repeated clock/circular-arrow icons mark timed vs. busy polling
encoding.emphasis: overlaying two arrow colors, black I/O flow and blue scheduling flow, on the same set of core boxes shows that Sandman's power-saving scheduler works alongside, not instead of, the normal polling I/O path
reusable_patterns: one coordinator core plus repeated identical worker cores, each independently wired to its own devices
a two-color arrow legend separating a control/scheduling flow from the underlying data/I-O flow on one diagram

evidence: Sandman categorizes CPU cores into two types: one main core and several worker cores
they both run in polling mode to process network- ing and storage I/O requests, and can communicate via event queues
It maintains a scheduler that gathers metrics and makes decisions to redistribute I/O threads among cores to save power

summary: Figure 6 is Sandman's system diagram, showing one Main Core and several Worker Cores that all run in polling mode to process networking and storage I/O, communicating via event queues. Only the Main Core additionally runs a Scheduler that gathers metrics and decides how to redistribute I/O threads across cores to save power. A legend distinguishes a black 'I/O Flow' from a blue 'Scheduling Flow': black arrows connect NIC and SSD devices below, via TX/RX and SQ/CQ, up to each core's I/O Thread, while blue arrows carry metric events from Worker Cores to the Main Core and decisions back down, with a separate bold arrow showing an I/O thread physically migrating between cores. Clock and circular-arrow icons further mark which components use timed versus busy polling.
summary_zh: 图6为Sandman系统图：主核心与工作核心均以轮询处理网络和存储I/O，经事件队列通信；仅主核心运行调度器，采集指标并决策线程迁移以省电。图例区分黑色I/O流与蓝色调度流，NIC/SSD经TX/RX、SQ/CQ接入各核心。
